paragraphs: This page groups the current public projects and older technical work.

AgenticCareerBoost combines portfolio infrastructure, reports, automation, and career tooling. P3CTeX is LaTeX/document tooling. AAAAT is separate job-search tooling derived from earlier ACB experiments. IronBank is older Java/Spring backend work from the banking simulation project.

items.title: AgenticCareerBoost
items.subtitle: Career engineering workspace combining a static portfolio, reports, automation, and application tooling.
items.summary: Repository-backed career tooling with a static site, LaTeX reports, CV material, application-tracking experiments, automation, and public project documentation.

blocks.lead: AgenticCareerBoost is a personal engineering workspace built around a real career-search workflow.
paragraphs: The repository combines a static portfolio, structured project content, LaTeX reports and CV sources, application-tracking experiments, GitHub Actions, validation scripts, and local utilities used during the job-search process.

AI-assisted workflows are one part of the system rather than the subject of the project: they operate alongside ordinary files, scripts, structured data, CI, and manually reviewable outputs. The repository also preserves enough development history to show how the implementation changed over time.

items.value: Static HTML/CSS/JavaScript and JSON-backed content published through GitHub Pages.
LaTeX sources and build paths for the public CV and technical reports.
Local tracker experiments and a JSON-to-LaTeX cover-letter renderer used during real applications.
Real application data, tailored CVs and letters, recruiter notes, raw offers, generated private PDFs, and databases remain local and untracked.

paragraphs: The Application Tracker is an earlier local implementation for storing opportunities, offer snapshots, call material, keyword definitions, and references to generated application artifacts.

Its public route uses fake data only. The current lightweight cover-letter path takes private JSON input and renders a LaTeX/PDF letter locally; the broader tracker work later informed the separate AAAAT project.

items.text: The project accumulated stale style, duplicated paths, old drafts, over-broad checks, and state/rule confusion that could steer later work badly.

items.text: The work paused with useful artifacts present but with campaign momentum and public explanation still uneven.

items.title: Launch Readiness Gap
items.text: The attempted restart showed that profile and social artifacts existed, but structure and evidence boundaries were not clean enough to present confidently.

items.title: Public Presentation Cleanup
items.text: The cleanup separated current guidance from historical evidence, kept discarded drafts out of future context, published formal reports, and made the first LinkedIn presentation possible.

items.title: Post-Launch Hardening
items.text: The public launch exposed sharper bugs: deployment-base routing, generated CV PDFs, static-file fallback loops, brittle checks, and the need to tighten CI scope around generated and hand-authored LaTeX outputs.

paragraphs: The current repository is intentionally narrower than its earlier iterations: the public website, CV, reports, application-tooling experiments, and selected historical material remain together because they document the same career-engineering workflow.
Older rules, tests, state files, and sprint notes are retained only as development history. Current work is ordinary repository maintenance: code, documents, site content, local utilities, and CI.
AAAAT and future CV-generation product work are developed separately rather than expanding ACB into a general-purpose job-search product.

items.subtitle: LaTeX tooling for reports, diagrams, listings, CV material, and repeatable document builds.
items.summary: LaTeX work for reports, CV material, diagrams, listings, screenshots, and document builds.

paragraphs: P3CTeX is my LaTeX class and package work for academic and technical documents.
It handles page structure, localized academic labels, code listings, screenshots, diagrams, covers, headers, report conventions, and CV/report builds.
It is document engineering for repeatable reports, CV material, and technical artifacts where source and rendered output need to stay aligned.

paragraphs: AAAAT is the separate Agent-Agnostic Auto Application Tracker project.
It continues the application-tracking direction first explored inside ACB, with the product work moved into its own repository rather than extending the ACB prototype indefinitely.
Its core direction is local-first storage for application data and tooling around reusable profile material and generated application artifacts.

The project covers accounts, users, transactions, permissions, services, and persistence.
Today I would document more, test more, and make the domain rules more explicit, but the project still marks the Java/Spring baseline.
